jj < fmaEnd; ++jj) s[jj] = std::fma(a, d[jj], s[jj]);\n    for (; jj < vecEnd; ++jj) s[jj] = mulAddScalar(s[jj], a, d[jj]);\n#endif\n    for (size_t j = vecEnd; j <= jmax; ++j) {\n        if ((j & ~static_cast<size_t>(3)) <= kk) s[j] = std::fma(a, d[j], s[j]);\n        else s[j] = mulAddScalar(s[j], a, d[j]);\n    }\n}\n\n'''+s[a:]\n\n# ---- finishRow: remove hasDiag path (now handled by the wavefront) ----\na=s.index(\"// Finish row i of the panel\")\nb=s.index(\"// Lightweight sense-reversing spin barrier\")\ns=s[:a]+r'''// Finish row i (below the diagonal block) of the panel [jb, jb+nb): for each panel column j\n// the full sum is   S_i[j-jb] + sum_{k=jb}^{j-1} L(i,k) L(j,k)   (k increasing), which is\n// accumulated for all columns at once: as soon as L(i,k) is final it is folded into the\n// running sums of every later column via the transposed diagonal block D,\n// D[kk][jj] = L(jb+jj, jb+kk) for jj > kk (lanes jj <= kk are zero / already consumed).\ninline void finishRow(double* __restrict__ Ai, const double* __restrict__ Si,\n                      const double* __restrict__ D, const double* __restrict__ diag,\n                      const size_t jb, const size_t nb, const size_t nbp) {\n    alignas(32) double s[NB + CB];\n    for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nbp; ++jj) s[jj] = Si[jj];\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < nb; ++kk) {\n        const double l = (Ai[jb + kk] - s[kk]) / diag[kk];\n        Ai[jb + kk] = l;\n        axpyRow(s, l, D + kk * nbp, nbp, kk);\n    }\n}\n\n// Row li of the diagonal block, executed concurrently with the other rows of the block\n// as a wavefront: step kk of row li may run once row li-1 has completed step kk\n// (prog[li-1] > kk), which by induction means every row < li has, so diag[kk] and\n// D[kk][jj] for jj < li are final. Progress is published after each step.\nstruct alignas(64) RowProgress {\n    std::atomic<int> v{-1};\n};\n\ninline bool diagRow(double* __restrict__ Ai, const double* __restrict__ Si, double* __restrict__ D,\n                    double* __restrict__ diag, RowProgress* prog, std::atomic<bool>& ok,\n                    const size_t jb, const size_t li, const size_t nbp) {\n    alignas(32) double s[NB + CB];\n    for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nbp; ++jj) s[jj] = Si[jj];\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < li; ++kk) {\n        while (prog[li - 1].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) <= static_cast<int>(kk)) _mm_pause();\n        const double l = (Ai[jb + kk] - s[kk]) / diag[kk];\n        Ai[jb + kk] = l;\n        D[kk * nbp + li] = l;\n        axpyRowUpTo(s, l, D + kk * nbp, li, kk);\n        prog[li].v.store(static_cast<int>(kk) + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n    }\n    const double val = Ai[jb + li] - s[li];\n    bool good = true;\n    if (val <= 0.0) {\n        if (ok.exchange(false)) {\n            printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", jb + li);\n        }\n        good = false;\n    } else {\n        Ai[jb + li] = sqrt(val);\n        diag[li] = Ai[jb + li];\n    }\n    prog[li].v.store(static_cast<int>(NB) + 1, std::memory_order_release);  // row done\n    return good;\n}\n\n'''+s[b:]\n\n# ---- choleskyDecomposition body ----\na=s.index(\"bool choleskyDecomposition(\")\nb=s.index(\"// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\")\ns=s[:a]+r'''bool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& Avec, const size_t n) {\n    double* __restrict__ A = Avec.data();\n    if (n == 0) return true;\n    std::atomic<bool> ok{true};\n\n    // Work buffers (cache-line aligned views into huge-page backed vectors)\n    std::vector<double> Pbuf[2], Sbuf, Dbuf, diagBuf;\n    allocateHugeVector(Pbuf[0], n * NB + 8);      // transposed panel: P[k][jj] = L(jb+jj, k), k < jb\n    allocateHugeVector(Pbuf[1], n * NB + 8);      // (double buffered: next panel is built during this one)\n    allocateHugeVector(Sbuf, (n + RB) * NB + 8);   // lanes jj <= kk are never written: stay zero\n    double* __restrict__ diag = diagBuf.data();\n    std::vector<RowProgress> prog(NB);            // wavefront progress of the diagonal block rows\n\n    const int nthreads = threadsFor(n);\n    SpinBarrier barrier(nthreads);\n    const size_t diagThreads = std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(nthreads), 16);\n\n#pragma omp parallel num_threads(nthreads)\n    {\n        const size_t T = static_cast<size_t>(nthreads);\n        const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n\n        // Rows are owned by threads in a block-cyclic fashion: row group G = i / RB belongs to\n        // thread G % T. The mapping is fixed for the whole factorization, so a thread keeps\n        // touching the same rows (cache locality) and the remaining work stays balanced.\n        auto firstGroup = [&](const size_t G0) { return G0 + ((t + T - G0 % T) % T); };\n\n        for (size_t jb = 0; jb < n; jb += NB) {\n            const size_t nb = std::min(NB, n - jb);  // columns in this panel\n            const size_t je = jb + nb;\n            const size_t nbp = ((nb + CB - 1) / CB) * CB;  // padded width (stride of P, S and D)\n            const size_t G0 = jb / RB;                     // first row group of this panel\n            const size_t nextNb = (je < n) ? std::min(NB, n - je) : 0;\n            const size_t nextNbp = ((nextNb + CB - 1) / CB) * CB;\n            const double* __restrict__ P = Pbufs[(jb / NB) & 1];\n            double* __restrict__ Pnext = Pbufs[((jb / NB) + 1) & 1];\n\n            // 1) Partial sums for every row i >= jb over the already-finished columns k < jb\n            //    (P[k][jj] = L(jb+jj, k) was transposed during the previous panel).\n            //    k is blocked so that the panel slice P[k0..k1) stays in L1 while a thread\n            //    sweeps all of its row groups. Only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable is still `cholesky`, and no new files or dependencies were added.\n\n**Results (default settings, 128 threads on this 2-socket EPYC 7763)**\n\n| n | original | new | relative error (-v) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms | 2–3 ms | 6e-14 |\n| 2048 | 2153 ms | 15 ms | |\n| 4096 | 17.9 s | 44 ms | |\n| 8192 | n/a | 181 ms (≈1 TFLOPS) | |\n\nScaling at n=4096 is near-linear to 32 threads (1377 ms → 74 ms) and continues to 44 ms at 128. The non-positive-definite error path prints the same message and exit code as the original.\n\n**What the new code does**\n\n- **Blocked left-looking factorization** in 64-column panels. The expensive partial sums (dot products over already-finished columns) run fully in parallel with rows owned block-cyclically by threads. The diagonal block runs as a row wavefront over 16 threads with atomic progress flags, and the remaining rows are finished in parallel.\n- **Bit-exact arithmetic.** Each element uses the same summation order as the original. I found that GCC compiles the original reduction as separately rounded multiply+add for the first floor(len/4)*4 terms and FMA for the tail. The AVX2 kernels reproduce exactly that, with an empty asm barrier to stop GCC from re-fusing the intrinsics. A plain-loop fallback compiles on non-AVX2 targets and validates.\n- **Cache and NUMA work.** A k-blocked kernel keeps the 16 KB panel slice in L1, the transposed next panel is built on the fly while rows are already in cache, and scratch buffers are mmap-backed, prefaulted, and NUMA-interleaved. The matrix allocation re-enables transparent huge pages via prctl because this host's service disables them per process, which was also causing tens of thousands of NUMA-balancing faults in the timed region.\n- **Thread setup.** When the user sets no binding policy, the program pins threads to physical cores and defaults to one thread per core.
